examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
I understand well (for a long time).
Today is a (for a long time) busy day.

meanings.note: Used as casual past (걸렸어.).

examples.text: 이제 다 됐어, 낙서 지우는 데 좀 시간이 걸렸어. 주차장 도착하면 다시 전화할게.
examples.trans: It is all finished now—scrubbing off the graffiti took a while. I will call again once I reach the parking lot.
Let us do that (it took) right away.

examples.text: 근데 너는 이 아파트에 언제부터 살았냐?
examples.trans: Anyway, how long have you lived in this apartment complex?
in this apartment complex in everyday conversation

meanings.note: noun

examples.trans: Go forward.
Do well in the future.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

examples.text: 어떤 한 사람이 나를 보게 만드는 것도 쉽지 않은데, 시청률을 얻는다는 건 어쩌면 사람의 마음을 얻는 일인 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: Even getting one person to look at me is far from easy—winning ratings seems like the art of winning people's hearts.

examples.text: 저 아파트 앞에서 진짜 일인 시위 합니다! 거기 너무 깜깜해서 위험하다니까요, 오늘부터 내가 확인합니다!
examples.trans: I will stage a one-man protest outside that apartment! It is pitch-dark and dangerous out there, so starting tonight I am checking every day!

examples.text: 저 아파트 앞에서 진짜 일인 시위 합니다! 거기 너무 깜깜해서 위험하다니까요, 오늘부터 내가 확인합니다!
examples.trans: I will stage a one-man protest outside that apartment! It is pitch-dark and dangerous out there, so starting tonight I am checking every day!
The topic of protest, demonstration came up in today's meeting.

meanings.note: Points to a place near the listener, and in casual or brisk speech is used to call out to someone whose name you do not know. RR: geogi.

examples.trans: Hey, you there, just a moment!
How is the atmosphere there?

meanings.note: Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.

examples.text: 저 아파트 앞에서 진짜 일인 시위 합니다! 거기 너무 깜깜해서 위험하다니까요, 오늘부터 내가 확인합니다!
examples.trans: I will stage a one-man protest outside that apartment! It is pitch-dark and dangerous out there, so starting tonight I am checking every day!
The mood on set today is truly because it is pitch-dark.

meanings.note: Used as adverbial -게 (위험하게,).

examples.text: 에이, 이 계집애가 밤늦게 위험하게, 아무튼 정말!
examples.trans: Ugh, this girl staying out so dangerously late at night—honestly!

examples.text: 회사가 신디 핸들링을 못 한다, 사이가 안 좋다, 재계약이 위험하다…
examples.trans: That the agency cannot manage Cindy, we are on bad terms, her contract renewal is in jeopardy…

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?
Let's checked together today.
I worked hard to checked yesterday too.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
